drafts.title: Ride stays composed on broken pavement and cabin remains quiet at highway speeds
drafts.description: When driving over broken or uneven pavement the car feels composed (not harsh) and at highway speeds above 70 mph wind noise is not distracting to driver or front passenger.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized broken-pavement test loop, peak vertical acceleration transmitted to the seats is reduced by ≥15% compared with the current 5 Series baseline; in a blinded user panel of 20 customers performing the same loop, at least 75% rate ride comfort ≥7/10. For highway aero noise, measured interior A-weighted sound pressure level at 75 mph (driver ear position, windows closed) is ≤68 dB(A).
assumptions: Comparable tire size/pressure and vehicle load are used for baseline and successor tests.
Standardized test sections for broken pavement will be selected and repeatable.
Interior noise targets assume common windshield, mirror and sealing geometry for the successor.
uncertainties: Noise and ride results depend on tire choice and exterior trim; some wheel/trim options may not achieve the target.
Very severe pavement conditions may still produce subjective harshness despite improvements.

drafts.title: Lane keeping assist steers smoothly in curves with no abrupt corrections
drafts.description: Lane keeping assist centers the car in the lane and applies steering corrections gradually so customers do not perceive sudden or nervous steering in curves.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a closed-course curved-lane validation (series of left/right curves at 35–70 mph), abrupt steering correction events—defined as lateral jerk spikes >0.5 m/s^3—are reduced by ≥75% versus the current 5 Series baseline; in a 30-run subjective evaluation, at least 90% of runs are rated by participants as having no abrupt steering correction.
assumptions: Baseline metrics from the current 5 Series are available for comparison.
Tests are run with reasonable lane markings and typical highway speeds; very degraded markings or snow/ice are out of scope for the acceptance test.
uncertainties: Performance in poor lane-marking or adverse weather conditions may remain limited by external sensor visibility and map data.
Improvements may require trade-offs with aggressive lane-centering in emergency scenarios.

drafts.title: Offer a long-range variant that delivers at least 600 miles real-world range on a single refuel/charge cycle
drafts.description: Customers can choose a 5 Series variant engineered for long trips that delivers at least 600 miles real-world driving range between refuels/charges, reducing the need for frequent stops on long journeys.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The long-range variant demonstrates ≥600 miles declared real-world range and completes two independent 600-mile validation drives (mixed highway/city, representative driving behavior) without requiring refuel/charge beyond planned stops determined by the vehicle's range management.
assumptions: The long-range outcome may be achieved by a plug-in-hybrid architecture (combined fuel + electric) or an unusually efficient BEV variant; successor product planning chooses the appropriate powertrain.
Validation drives are conducted with typical luggage and two occupants and common driving styles for long trips.
Fuel/energy quality and available infrastructure are comparable to today.
uncertainties: Achieving 600 miles may increase weight or reduce cabin/package space in some variants.
Customer real-world range will vary with driving style, climate control use, and route profile.

drafts.title: Find compatible fast chargers on trips and show charging state at a glance at the charge port
drafts.description: While planning or driving long routes the car shows chargers that are compatible with the vehicle (plug type and accepted payment/roaming) and the charge port has a visible indicator that clearly shows charging states (charging, full, fault) readable from about 3 meters.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a 200-mile route test the vehicle's charger planner lists compatible fast chargers along the route and at least 90% of listed chargers successfully start a charging session in field checks; the charge-port indicator displays distinct visual states for Charging / Full / Fault and is clearly readable from 3 meters in daylight.
assumptions: Backend charger data and roaming/payment agreements are available for the regions tested.
Field checks use a representative sample of public fast chargers in the region.
uncertainties: Third-party charger outages or inaccurate operator data can reduce effective compatibility despite correct planner behavior.
Visual readability of the port indicator can be affected by installation height and ambient lighting.

drafts.title: Allow noticeably faster AC charging at destination/home where 22 kW three-phase AC is available
drafts.description: When the car is connected to a compatible three-phase AC supply at home or at a destination, customers experience substantially shorter plug-in times compared with current models.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: When connected to a 22 kW three-phase AC supply, the vehicle reduces 0→80% replenishment time by ≥40% compared with the current 5 Series, verified in repeatable charging tests on a 22 kW supply.
assumptions: 22 kW three-phase AC supplies are available at the tested charging location.
Successor vehicle power electronics are designed to accept higher AC power where grid wiring and connectors permit.
uncertainties: Many home installations lack three-phase wiring; actual customer benefit depends on local electrical infrastructure.
Some public destination chargers may report lower than rated power due to site wiring limitations.

drafts.title: Type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the vehicle obtains type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request logged for homologation process; actual approval depends on regulatory authorities and OEM submission.
assumptions: Homologation and type-approval processes are governed by national authorities and are external to product requirement definition.
uncertainties: Timing and outcome depend entirely on regulatory decisions and technical compliance evidence.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory type approval is a homologation activity outside product requirement scope; customers asked for approval rather than a product behaviour.

drafts.title: Compliance with CARB emission limits across US states (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the powertrain complies with California (CARB) emission limits in all US states.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request captured for engineering and compliance teams; verification and certification depend on regulatory testing and approvals.
assumptions: Emissions certification and legal compliance are handled by regulatory homologation teams and are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
uncertainties: Certification paths and timelines vary by jurisdiction and are not determined here.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory certification is out of scope for product requirement drafts.

drafts.title: UN R155 cybersecurity type approval (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the vehicle fulfils UN R155 cybersecurity type approval.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request recorded for compliance; actual approval depends on security evidence and certification bodies.
assumptions: Certification activity and evidence collection are handled by compliance teams; the request is out of scope for customer-facing functional requirements.
uncertainties: Requirements or test outcomes from certification authorities may evolve.
drafts.scope_reason: Security type approval is a regulatory/certification task outside product feature definition.

drafts.title: Battery passport (EU regulation) compliance (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request captured; evidence and compliance depend on regulatory reporting and supplier data.
assumptions: Compliance requires supplier data and regulatory reporting processes; this is a legal/regulatory matter handled separately.
uncertainties: Timing and scope of the battery passport requirements may change with regulation updates.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory reporting/compliance is out of scope for product requirement definition.

drafts.title: 800 V electrical architecture request
drafts.description: Customers request that the car uses an 800 V electrical architecture.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request captured for architecture review; technical feasibility and decision are engineering scope items.
assumptions: High-voltage architecture decisions require detailed engineering and supplier alignment; this draft records the customer ask but is not a customer-facing functional requirement.
uncertainties: Architecture impacts weight, cost and supplier choices; outcomes are uncertain at this stage.
drafts.scope_reason: Request names a specific electrical architecture (engineering specification) which is out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Solid-state cells with 400 Wh/kg (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the battery uses solid-state cells with 400 Wh/kg energy density.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request noted; materials and cell chemistry specifications are engineering/supplier decisions.
assumptions: Cell chemistry and specific energy targets are engineering-level specifications requiring supplier validation.
uncertainties: Availability, cost and manufacturability of such cells at scale are uncertain within 3–5 years.
drafts.scope_reason: A request for a specific cell chemistry and energy density is an engineering specification; we log it but treat it out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Front brake disc diameter 395 mm (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the front brake discs have a diameter of 395 mm.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request recorded; specific component dimensions are engineering choices.
assumptions: Brake component sizing impacts weight, package and NVH and is an engineering trade-off.
uncertainties: Actual effective braking feel depends on calipers, pads and vehicle tuning, not just disc diameter.
drafts.scope_reason: Explicit component dimension request is an engineering specification out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Preferred LiDAR supplier for highway assist (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers ask that highway assist uses a LiDAR sensor from a named supplier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer supplier preference logged for procurement discussion; supplier selection is out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.
assumptions: Supplier selection and sensor architecture are engineering/procurement responsibilities.
uncertainties: Supplier availability, cost and integration feasibility may change over time.
drafts.scope_reason: Request names a supplier (procurement/engineering detail) and is out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
